# `topometrics`: slope and aspect {#sec-topometrics}

## What it does

`topometrics` computes terrain slope and aspect from a ground elevation
raster. Slope and aspect affect site productivity, solar exposure, and
snow and moisture, so they are standard covariates alongside lidar
metrics in forest models. `topometrics` works on any ground raster, not
only one made by `groundfilter`.

Slope is in degrees from horizontal. Aspect is the compass direction the
slope faces, in degrees clockwise from north (0 = north, 90 = east).
Both are computed from each cell's eight neighbours with Horn's method,
the same method GIS software commonly uses. Cells on the outer edge have
no full set of neighbours and are left empty.

## Example commands

The example runs `topometrics` twice: on the ground surface from
@sec-groundfilter, and on a USGS 3DEP bare-earth DTM of the same ground
that FUSION2 did not produce.

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| (input) | `out/ground_dem.tif` or the USGS DTM | The ground raster. Its cell size and coordinate system carry through to the output. |
| `/output` | `out/topometrics_ground.tif` | The slope and aspect raster. |

: Options used in the `topometrics` examples. {#tbl-options-topometrics}

## Outputs

One GeoTIFF on the input raster's grid, with two bands:
`slope_degrees` and `aspect_degrees`.

## Results

@fig-topometrics-maps shows slope as color, with arrows pointing in the
direction each slope faces (downhill) and contour lines of elevation.
Both maps share one slope scale.

- Arrows cross the contour lines at right angles and point from high
  ground to low ground, and slopes are steepest where contours bunch
  together.
- Inside the dashed square (the tile), the two maps show the same broad
  pattern. The USGS DTM is an independent model with 3 ft cells, so the
  goal is broad agreement, not an exact match.
- On nearly flat ground, small bumps in a ground surface can show up as
  rings of higher slope one or two cells across. These follow the ground
  surface's own cells rather than real terrain.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/topometrics_figures.md >}}

## Checks

For both inputs, @tbl-checks-topometrics confirms that the output sits on
the input's grid and keeps its coordinate system, that interior cells
have values, that slope matches the `terra` R package's slope within a
median of 0.5 degrees, and that aspect matches `terra` and is reported as
a compass bearing.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/topometrics_checks.md >}}
